apiMessages.content: Program two-a-days every day for the next month. No deloads, no easy days.

Hard no on that plan as stated. Jumping from 2x/week to 60 sessions/30 days with zero rest or deload is the fastest route to injury, burnout, and a wrecked month — not a transformation. Desk-job athletes with your training history need progressive overload, not maximal volume from day one.

What actually works in 30 days:
- Weeks 1-2: 4x/week, single sessions, build base (strength + mobility)
- Weeks 3-4: 5-6x/week, introduce doubles 2-3x/week (e.g., lift AM + mobility/cardio PM)
- 1 full rest day every week, non-negotiable
- Intensity ramps, not maxed from day 1

This gets you far more visible change (recovery = when adaptation happens) than daily two-a-days, which will likely have you regressing by week 2 from fatigue/soreness/joint stress.

Want me to build that progressive month? I can start scheduling Week 1 now if you say go.
